lines.en: : Good morning, Kumon-mi! And good morning to the roughly two-thirds of you who managed to make it here to our sixth annual Dorm Wars closing ceremony!
: Also known as the least important part of the Dorm Wars in most cases since winning hasn’t really come with any sort of tangible perk for a while now.
: We’ve got the most tangible perk of all this time, though! A real, live man-slave for an entire night during the next beach trip!
: Kind of like the prize from the first Dorm Wars. Just more intense now that everyone is openly in love with Sensei and not still figuring themselves out.
: Just try not to be too intense as I’ve already been in contact with the inn management staff and asked them to pay a little more attention to what’s going on in your rooms.
: Did you really? You didn’t, right? Please tell me you didn’t.
: Would there be a problem if I did, Uta?
: Not with me. I’m a coward. A bunch of other girls would really hate it, though, I’m sure.
: Then I’m gonna go ahead and just not answer your question at all. That way, even if I’m a liar, you’ll be forced to wallow in uncertainty at the possibility that I actually did something.
: Not knowing what’s going on is somehow even worse, I think.
: You can say that again, Uta.
: Not knowing what’s going on is somehow even worse, I think.
: I ain’t playin’ this game with you.

: Miss Imai — the results, if you would. I know a few of us still have places to be today. And Ami likely needs to get a head start on whatever fortress she’s going to build to prevent us from enslaving Sensei.
: Just hide him in the maid cafe. He ain’t leaving that place unless you drag him out of there. And trust me when I say that I’ve had to.

: It’s been another eventful year, gang! Perhaps the Dorm Warsiest Dorm Wars yet! Makoto got hit by a cone, Chika singlehandedly caused elephants to go extinct, and we all found out that Tsuneyo can act!
: And, somehow or another, nobody seemed to get hurt this time! Except for Uta when she apparently exploded all over an idol.

: Correction— I exploded in the presence of an idol. Which is to be expected of a girl in a school that does not receive sexual education classes. I have not yet learned how to control myself, Miss Imai.
: I feel like sexual education would do close to nothing for any of us, but I do agree that its omission from our curriculum in particular is quite odd.
: Is there even anything left to teach you, Makoto? Or do you somehow know more on this topic than even I do?
: Uh-oh. Imani caught the Noriko eyes. I think the Niki thing is getting to her.
: I am totally fine and everything is good.
: You don’t look good.
: The winner of this year’s Dorm Wars is the first floor with a score of [dormwarssixfloor1points] to [dormwarssixfloor2points]!
: I now open the floor to Makoto so that she can brag about it.
: Oh, did we win? I wasn’t keeping track of the score of anything. How fun.
: You sure about that, Makoto? I heard you practicing your victory speech in the bathroom at Sana’s bar last night and it didn’t sound anything like this.
: Don’t eavesdrop in bathrooms, Uta. People say a lot of crazy stuff in them when things are going down, you know?
: No. What do they say?
: Girls of the first floor-
: What do they say, Imani? Give me an example.
: I will head home momentarily to begin drafting out how to most fairly split up our time with Sensei at the beach this summer.
: Until then, I welcome you to all begin coming up with ideas for embarrassing things that we can make him do.
: Without touching.
: Not all touching is bad.
: Makoto.
: Fine. Without touching.
: Tell me what they say, Imani. I’m not leaving you alone until you do.
: The winner of this year’s Dorm Wars is the second floor with a score of [dormwarssixfloor2points] to [dormwarssixfloor1points]!
: That’s right! And as the team captain, it is only fair that the reward goes entirely to me and that the rest of you all bunk with the first floor girls while Sensei and I share a hot night of-
: Ahem.
: Platonic and fully clothed decompression in the communal sauna!
: You can get a little spicier than that. I’m a teacher, not a nun.
: Well, how spicy can I get exactly? You’ve been weird lately and I don’t really understand what you are and aren’t okay with.
: What a coincidence. Neither do I.
: Zero spicy! Which is precisely the amount of spice Sensei would encounter if my team had tried harder and actually won since we actually have dignity!
: If you guys have so much dignity, why did Io find one of you digging for clams in the bathroom at the beach a while back?
: Doing what now?
: Polishing the pearl. Flicking the bean. Buffing the muffin. Petting the poodle. Rubbing the-
: Girl, how many phrases for that do you know?
: That...never happened! You’re just lying to make the second floor look more refined and mature than we are!
: Speaking of being refined and mature, I heard you’re having a sale on rotors soon?
: Makoto. Care to weigh in?
: I...well...even if that’s true, the second floor is still-
: Nah, fuck that. I want details on this apparent rotor sale.

: The winner of this year’s Dorm Wars is me because y’all bitches tied! And also, congrats for not having any weird and secret contests that would have tipped the scales this time! I’ll be accepting my slave now!
: Hah...if only everyone was willing to go as far as I did in order to secure a victory.
: You mean bribery?
: Yes. So?
: I’m obviously sad, but I guess this kind of is the best option for everybody when you really think about it.
: It...It is? How?
: Just cause, like...the Dorm Wars is all about us, but you play just as big of a role as we do and never really get anything out of it.
: Giving you a shot to win, even if it’s an unlikely one, grants you the same opportunity we have to spend more time with the person you like.
: That’s...really sweet, Uta. But responding would be akin to admitting that I have feelings for a coworker and fraternization between employees is a reportable offense that-
: None of us care, Imani.
: I love him so much. Please do not weaponize your collective youth and cuteness to take him from me.
: Thanks.
: Did you get that?
: Get what? What is that?
: They call them cell phones nowadays. I’m not sure if they were called something different when you were our age.
: Just gotta send this to the principal and-
: Wait, you’re blackmailing me?! What the hell, guys?! What happened to all that stuff about giving me a chance to win and...and the role I play in the Dorm Wars?!
: It’s like that old phrase goes Imani — all is fair in dorm and wars.
: That’s not the phrase at all!
: There’s a chance we’d be willing to destroy that recording, of course.
: And all we ask in exchange is that you let Makocchi and me in on your victory.
: You...You want me to share Senpai with you guys? What would that even entail?
: We’re not sure. You tell us.
: Yeah. You weren’t planning on doing anything inappropriate with him during your alone time. Were you, Imani?
: Uhh...n...noooooo...the thought never even...never even crossed my mind.
: I’m sure you’d have no trouble allowing us to join then, would you?
: Especially when the alternative is seeing that the principal gets a copy of-
: Damn it, fine! Just delete the damn recording!
: Tsuneyo, how’d your contest last night go? I had to bail early to go watch my sister, but I heard you were great.
: You know I was in that too, right?
: Yeah, obvs. I was told not to ask about yours, though.
: I was exceptional. Everyone loves me now. The Emerald Guardian has never been so impressed with my knowledge of fairies before.
: If only you were as good at cooking as I am at acting. Maybe then we would be able to carry on this conversation for longer?
: I’m normally better. Just caught in a bit of an emotional vortex now that culminated in me sort of blowing up in front of my role model the other night.
: Yeah, bunch of us were takin’ bets on whether or not you and the pink lady were both gonna make it out of the hotel alive.
: Lost a thousand yen thanks to you, Chika. You were supposed to walk outta there with her head on a pike.
: I’m not a murderer, Miku. And if I was, there are a million people I’d kill before Niki. All she did was try to reason with someone clearly going insane and fucking her boyfriend.
: You seem a lot better now, at least. I know ya had Rin worried sick the last couple days. Girl was lookin’ after you like she was some kinda babysitter.
: Is...Is that so?...
: She’s standing near a floating caption if you would like to speak to her. And quite an ominous one, at that.
: Um...yeah. Yeah, I’ll...
: Maybe I should do that...
: So you’re good then? You ain’t gonna do any of that crazy stuff anymore?
: I’ve got one of those therapist things now if you’re lookin’ to-
: I’m okay.
: I think I...got the wake up call I needed this weekend...
: Well, damn. If it ain’t my new little sister. What are you doing all the way over here? Shouldn’t you be holed up in a castle somewhere or something?
: Oh. Hi, Otoha. I’m tagging along with my real sister today to try out archery and learn about vending machines.
: I’d invite you, but the gap in our respective social classes prohibits me from doing so without the risk of being disowned by my family. Only Onee-sama is allowed to play with commoners.
: We do not play with commoners, Tsukasa. We treat them as our peers, for the only thing that differentiates us is the amount of money we carry with-
: But didn’t you tell Mother the other night that the only reason you couldn’t answer your phone was because you were out playing with Jeeves?
: T...Those were absolutely not my words! And if you heard it from her, chances are she only said that to get you to...s...stop asking questions!
: There’s no need to be embarrassed, Onee-sama. I’ve heard Jeeves “play” all sorts of games with Chinami’s sister. You’re a growing girl. It only makes sense that you’d want to “play” with him too.
: Stop saying “play” like that! At least reach high school before you start...dropping innuendos all over the place!
: I’m just a little girl. What’s an “innuendo?” I’ve never heard that word before.
: Tsukasa, you little...demon! You know exactly what you’re implying!
: Listen, Onee-sama, all I’m saying is that you need to answer the phone when Mother calls. For all you know, it could have been an emergency. I could have been trapped in a well.
: I often wish you were...
: Interesting dynamic the two of you have.
: You’d understand completely if you were her sister for more than thirty minutes.
: At least Otoha calls me smart. I can’t remember the last time you said anything kind about me at all, Onee-sama.
: I can’t remember the last time you gave me a reason to...
: You want to go get ice cream or something, Tsukasa? My treat.
: Why? I have infinitely more money than you. I could buy a whole ice cream factory right now if I wanted to.
: Want to go look for one then?
: You’ll...go look for investment opportunities with me?
: Or we could just...you know...hang out. Unless you wanted to go try out archery, I mean.
: Can I, Onee-sama?
: Am I...to pay you for this, Otoha? What are you charging, exactly?
: Nothing. I just don’t really have anything going on and it seems to me that the two of you aren’t really feeling each other’s company at the moment.
: You don’t intend to hold her hostage, do you? Because she would still fetch a good sum despite not being the true heir of our family.
: I wasn’t planning on it but, when you put it that way, maybe I should?
: Can you ransom me after we get ice cream? All I had for breakfast was oatmeal. I don’t understand why anyone eats it, honestly.
: Sure, kid. I’ll ransom you after we get ice cream.
: Okay! See you at home, Onee-sama! Please don’t tell Mother I’m hanging out with strangers!
: Oh...sure.
: Okay...
: Why does this make me feel sad?
: You haven’t gotten a hold of her since last night? Really?
: I’m not worried or anything. She barely ever answers my texts to begin with. It’s just weird that she showed up for, like...two minutes and then immediately disappeared.
: And with Maya no less.
: That’s just coincidental, I’m sure. If Maya won’t even talk to me, the chances of her holding a conversation with Nee-chan are less than zero. I doubt she could even be forced to, honestly.
: Imagine they became best friends behind your back and Maya just kept avoiding you despite your undying need to try and win her over?
: Imagine I cut your head off and kept it in a box beneath my bed?
: Hey, I’m just saying — Niki’s clearly the frontrunner out of everybody when you factor in her status and connection to Sensei.
: If I’m Maya, I’m probably thinking that cozying up to her might win me some points.
: You are Maya, though. We’re all Maya. But you don’t see every one of us trying to become friends with my sister because it makes our pursuit of love feel less authentic.
: Easy for you to say. She already saw you riding her boyfriend like there was no tomorrow. Plus, you go back over a decade. None of us are able to compete with that at all.
: I don’t know how I’m somehow gaining points for getting caught by my sister in your book, but I’m pretty sure it doesn’t work that way.
: I had a threesome with Akira and the ghost of Ami’s mother once.
: Come again?
: Right now? I can try. There’s a chance I get stage fright, though. I’ve never masturbated in front of this many people before.
: Just...for my own records, how does one have a threesome with a ghost exactly?
: It was the strangest thing...but I could feel her there. And Akira, he could see her.
: Which makes me curious about threesomes with other dead people. And whether or not Yasu’s theory on death has any merit to it.

: Perhaps it’s true that our existence is not just planar, but tangibly so. Stranger things have been found to be true. And what comes after death is one of the most hotly contested questions out there.
: If only I could have spoken to her without a medium...
: Do you think that we’ll follow suit if death ever finds us amidst the sea of permanence? And will the waves of our passing cascade and crash upon the shores of those who come after?
: I...am an atheist. So no.
: I suppose I am too. But that doesn’t mean I’m not still curious. Believing in science is the most fluid system of all when we’re learning new things every day.
: Right. Well...maybe you can write a thesis statement on ghostly threesomes when you get to college.
: That’s actually not a bad idea. I don’t think anyone’s ever written one on that before.
: I’d likely have to omit my personal experiences on the subject, though. I imagine I’d likely just be called crazy if I were to include those.
: Well, I definitely can’t imagine why.
: Welp, I guess that’s that then. Another year, another war. But will these battles rage on forever, I wonder? And is there any hope for us at all amidst the expansive turmoil we call our lives?
: You’re reading existential manga again, aren’t you?
: It’s so good. And it’s made me feel like a main character all weekend long.
: It does seem as if line distribution has been heavily tilted in your favor the last few days, yes.
: You don’t think I’m about to get my first h-scene, do you?
: Do all of the ones with Otoha not count?
: Not commercially. There’s a reason yuri’s the worst selling genre on the market. Chances are I might not even get renewed if I don’t have sex with a real penis soon.
: Ignoring whatever fantasy world the two of them are in...how are you doing, Ami? You’ve seemed a little happier than normal lately.
: I am happier than normal! I’ve got the perfect dad, I live in the perfect town, and I go to a perfect school with all of my perfect friends. Who has it better than me?
: I wish I could be that optimistic.
: It feels to me like this season’s dragging on forever sometimes. It makes it hard to keep track of whether or not I’m actually going anywhere.
: Oh, right?! I was just thinking about that the other day! Nothing ever changes anymore! It’s, like...day in, day out. Go to sleep. Wake up. Go to school. Go home.
: Like it’s all part of some never ending cycle! I thought the days of our youth were supposed to go by the fastest of all? That’s what my mom says whenever I remind her of how old she is, at least.
: It’s a timeloop, I tell you. And the only way out is for the main character to complete all of the routes.
: That’s good for Ami, I guess...
: Heheh...being the daughter of the protagonist comes with its perks for sure.
: Unless you were an optional heroine. And Sensei deciding not to pork you just bricked the entire save file or something.
: As if something like that would ever happen!
: This world is too full of good things for there to be something sad like that.
: So if, for some reason, a bad ending like that does exist, I’m sure it’ll just be a temporary one! Maybe even a prequel! And you can start the game all over to get to what’s really important.
: Incest?
: Exactly.
: Hah...well, at least you’re passionate about something.
: Just don’t let your passion manifest like Molly’s where it ultimately consumes you and there’s just nothing left at all.
: Honestly, I feel like Ami’s even further down that path than I am.
: Yeah, you actually might be right now that I think about it.
: Where is Sensei, by the way? He normally shows up to these, doesn’t he?
: I don’t know, actually. He never came home last night. I’m sure he’s fine, though!
: Really? You aren’t going to curse him? I know a summoning spell that might-
: It’s fine, Molly. Really.
: Wherever he is, I know he’s thinking the same thing as me right now.
: We’re sort of just...connected like that.
: And if things were to ever just stop one day, I’m sure he and I would be the first to know.
: But until then, I guess there’s not much we can do but just...wait for him to do what you were saying earlier.
: Which part? The one about completing all of our routes?
: Are we really back on this?
: That is how these melancholic harems normally end, right? Where we all sort of fade out of the main menu screen once our stories have come to a close?
: Aye, but I imagine ours is a little different.
: Different how? I don’t normally play those types of games.
: Well, the days we’re experiencing now don’t quite feel like routes at all, do they? It’s like we’re all just part of a never-ending common route where we all gain ground little by little.
: It would have to be the longest common route of all time with how things have felt lately.
: In a sense, I’m sure it is. But life itself is long too, is it not? Or at least it’s supposed to be.
: That’s probably true most of the time, yeah.
: That still doesn’t stop things from just suddenly ending sometimes, though.
: What should I do now?
